title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.176): X is a smooth complex analytic space with a normal crossings divisor D. It is stratified by locally closed smooth strata D^*_{d_*} (d_* = (d_0,...,d_r) a flag of multiplicities). Grothendieck is building a homotopy-theoretic 'dissection' of X into elementary 'pieces of construction', in the spirit of tubular neighbourhoods or real oriented blow-up.

Over a stratum D^*_{d_*}, take the normal bundle Ň_{d_*} relative to D^*_{d_*} -> D_{d_0}. It splits locally into line bundles, one per branch. Choose the sub-fibration Ň_{d_*,(d'_0,d''_0)} for a pair d''_0 < d'_0, and remove the coordinate hyperplanes. The result Ň^* is a locally trivial bundle over D^*_{d_*} with fibre (C^*)^{d'_0-d''_0}.

The spaces V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} are the corresponding pieces of the dissection, roughly deleted tubular neighbourhoods of strata.

On this page Grothendieck says one must define a canonical equivalence of fundamental groupoids (295): Π_1(Ň^*_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)} | D^*_{d_*}) ≃ Π_1 V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0}. He names the left side Ň^{**}.

He then remarks in passing that knowing Π_1 V up to equivalence amounts to knowing the π_1 of Ň^* over each connected component of D^*_{d_*}. By the homotopy exact sequence of the torus fibration,
π_2(D^*) -> Z^r = π_1((C^*)^r) -> π_1(Ň^*) -> π_1(D^*) -> 1,
these are extensions of π_1 of the components of D^*_{d_*} by the quotients Z^r / ∂π_2.

The page serves the project of the next page: when all strata are K(π,1), as in the Teichmüller / M̄_{g,ν} situation, the system of these groupoids, with their canonical maps, should reconstruct the (pro)fundamental groupoid of X and the homotopy types of the associated 'neighbouring' topoi.

In the moduli case, π_2 = 0, so π_1 of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum is an extension of the stratum's π_1 (mapping class groups of the pieces) by the free abelian group of Dehn twists. This is the stabilizer of a multicurve, the 'structure at infinity' of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: Notational slip: the fibre rank is d'_0 - d''_0 (per p.176), but the page writes Z^r. Here r is not the length of the flag d_* = (d_0,...,d_r).

The extension need not be central. If the normal crossings divisor is not strict, monodromy can permute the branches and so act on Z^r. Even with trivial permutation, the action of π_1(base) on π_1 of the torus fibre is generally trivial only up to such permutations. The page does not address this.
The boundary map ∂: π_2(D^*) -> Z^r is not identified on the page. It is given by pairing (via Hurewicz) with the Chern classes of the branch line bundles. This is implicit, not an error.
The equivalence (295) is announced as something 'to be defined', not proved. Its precise meaning depends on the exact definition of V, which lies outside this page.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a punctured normal (torus) bundle of a stratum identified with that of the corresponding piece of a tubular dissection.
ideas.modern_name: Deleted tubular neighbourhood / link of a stratum; real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama log space) boundary pieces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical tubular-neighbourhood theory (Thom, Mather); for log geometry, Kato–Nakayama (1999)
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) on the structure at infinity of M_{g,n}

ideas.what: π_1 of the punctured normal bundle as an extension of π_1(stratum) by Z^r modulo the image of π_2, via the homotopy exact sequence.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy long exact sequence for a torus bundle; Euler/Chern class as boundary map

ideas.what: In the K(π,1) (Teichmüller) case, this extension is the stabilizer of a multicurve: mapping class group of the pieces extended by the free abelian group of Dehn twists.
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizers of multicurves / boundary strata groups of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, 'structure à l'infini')

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step: a fibration exact-sequence computation and an announced groupoid equivalence for deleted tubular neighbourhoods. The broader programme of reconstructing homotopy types from a system of stratum groupoids (exit-path or stratified homotopy, 'topos voisins') is interesting historically. But it appears on the next page and is anticipated by the Esquisse and later stratified-homotopy theory (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie).
